name: Text field
summary: A label, an optional hint, an input and a message. The base for the other fields.

when: For short text that has no more specific field.

anatomy.description: An error, or a note about what was understood.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's label. Pass a catalogue string.

props.name: hint
props.description: Help under the label, such as an example. Pass a catalogue string.

props.name: error
props.description: The error message. Setting it marks the field invalid; clearing it marks it valid. The app validates.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the form submits the value under.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether it must be filled in. Screen readers say so; the app checks it.

props.name: autocomplete
props.description: What the browser can fill in, such as name. Helps password managers and autofill.

states.name: Focus
states.description: A 2px focus ring, and a darker border.

states.name: Invalid
states.description: A red border and surface, and the error message under it.

states.name: Autofilled
states.description: Filled by the browser, in the theme's colours.

events.name: doras-input
events.when: The value changes, but never while text is still being composed with an input method, such as Japanese. Once a field has an error, validate live on this.

events.name: change
events.when: Someone leaves the field after changing it.

accessibility.name: Its label, which is a real label element tied to the input.

keyboard.action: Submits the form, as in a native form.

screenReader: Announced with its label, then its hint and any message, which are tied to it with aria-describedby.
When it has an error, it's announced as invalid, and the message is read with “Error:” before it.
announcements: Messages are announced politely as they change, so fixing an error is heard.
notes: Validation happens on submit, then live as people fix errors. The app decides; the field shows the result.
Autofilled values keep the theme's colours.

related.relationship: Lists every field's error on submit.

guidelines: Labels are short nouns, such as “Email address”.
Hints give an example, not instructions.
Error messages say what to do: “Enter your email address”, not “Invalid input”.

dosAndDonts.do: Keep the label visible above the field.
dosAndDonts.dont: Use placeholder text as the label.

dosAndDonts.do: Say how to fix an error.

evidence.point: Errors tied to the field with aria-describedby, and an “Error:” prefix, so screen reader users hear what's wrong and where.
Validating on submit, then live, is the least stressful timing (decision in #1).
